lemma: If a row h belongs to exactly four of the five P0 quads Q0,...,Q4, and j is the missing quad index, at least TWO distinct rows must have P0-quad membership exactly {j}. Otherwise this exact all-P1,L=0 case is impossible.
proof_steps: One P0 column contributes C(4,2)+5*C(3,2)=21 agreeing row-pairs; one P1 column contributes2*C(4,2)+3*C(3,2)+C(2,2)=22. Hence total agreements are5*21+3*22=171=C(19,2). Since no row-pair agrees more than once, EVERY row-pair agrees exactly once.
For any row r, summing its group-size-minus-one over all8 columns therefore equals18: it agrees once with each of its18 other rows.

For the row h of the lemma, the five P0 contributions are four3s and one2, totaling14. Its three P1 contributions must sum4. Each P1 contribution is1,2,or3, so their multiset is exactly{1,1,2}. Thus h is in the size2 group in exactly TWO P1 columns, and in a size3 group in the third.
Let u and v be h's two partners in these two size2 groups. They are DISTINCT: otherwise the same row-pair would agree in two P1 columns, contrary to the defining condition.

Each partner must avoid all four P0 quads containing h, since membership in any such quad would give that row-pair an additional agreement. Thus each partner's P0-quad membership is either empty or exactly{j}.

A row with empty P0-quad membership has P0 contribution5*2=10, hence needs P1 contribution8. But if it is paired with h in one P1 column, its three P1 contributions sum at most1+3+3=7, a contradiction. Neither u nor v can have empty membership.
Therefore u and v are two distinct rows with P0-quad membership exactly{j}. This proves the lemma without any enumeration, placement-list, solver, proof-stream or encoder premise.

For b30, h has membership{0,1,2,3} and j=4. Q4 has size4; the other nonsingleton memberships{1,4},{2,4},{3,4} occupy three DISTINCT rows of Q4. Hence exactly ONE Q4 row has membership{4}, contradicting the required TWO.
For b44, h again has membership{0,1,2,3},j=4. The memberships{0,4},{1,4},{2,4},{3,4} occupy all four DISTINCT rows of Q4. Hence ZERO rows have membership{4}, again a contradiction.
